When acalabrutinib is co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, it is recommended to temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment if the strong CYP3A inhibitor is used for a short duration (e.g., up to 7 days). 2. Adagrasib increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 3. Adagrasib, a CYP3A4 substrate, should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until adagrasib concentrations reach steady-state (~8 days). If steady-state is not achieved, co-administration increases adagrasib concentrations and toxicity risks. 4. Posaconazole increases adagrasib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Both adagrasib and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes, serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. If co-administration is unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended. 6. Posaconazole increases ado-trastuzumab emtansine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Posaconazole increases afatinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If co-administered, reduce the afatinib daily dose by 10 mg if not tolerated, and monitor closely. 8. Both albuterol and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Posaconazole increases alfentanil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 10. Both alfuzosin and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Posaconazole increases aliskiren levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 12. Posaconazole increases almotriptan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Posaconazole increases alosetron levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 14. Posaconazole increases alprazolam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Aluminum hydroxide decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Posaconazole increases ambrisentan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 17. Posaconazole decreases amikacin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 18. Posaconazole increases amiodarone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and amiodarone increases posaconazole levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 19. Both amisulpride and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Posaconazole increases amitriptyline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. Both drugs increase the QTc interval, so therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 21. Posaconazole increases amlodipine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Amobarbital decreases posaconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 23. Both amoxapine and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 24. Both anagrelide and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug used. 25. Posaconazole increases apalutamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. 26. Posaconazole increases apixaban levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug used. 27. Posaconazole increases aprepitant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Both arformoterol and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Posaconazole increases aripiprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of QTc prolongation. 30. Posaconazole increases armodafinil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 31. Both arsenic trioxide and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug used. 32. Both artemether and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 33. Posaconazole increases artemether/lumefantrine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval, so therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 34. Both asenapine and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 35. Posaconazole increases atazanavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 36. Posaconazole increases atogepant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. The recommended atogepant dose is 10 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 37. Both atomoxetine and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Posaconazole increases atorvastatin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Posaconazole increases avanafil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse events, including hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. 40. Posaconazole increases avapritinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug used. 41. Posaconazole increases axitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. 42. Both azithromycin and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 43. Posaconazole increases bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Posaconazole and bedaquiline both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring, including ECG, is recommended. 45. Posaconazole increases bedaquiline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefit outweighs the risk. 46. Posaconazole increases benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended due to the risk of fatal respiratory depression. 47. Posaconazole increases berotralstat levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust the P-gp substrate dose if co-administered. 48. Posaconazole increases betrixaban levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily if co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. 49. Posaconazole increases bexarotene levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Posaconazole increases bortezomib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Posaconazole increases bosentan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 52. Posaconazole increases bosutinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug used. 53. Posaconazole increases brentuximab vedotin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse reactions. 54. Posaconazole increases brexpiprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 55. Posaconazole increases brigatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug used. If unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by 50%. 56. Posaconazole increases bromocriptine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 57. Posaconazole increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Posaconazole increases buprenorphine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval, and co-administration is contraindicated. 59. Posaconazole increases buspirone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Posaconazole increases busulfan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Butabarbital decreases posaconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised.
